subject: Autoscale policy starvation — impact summary and scheduled mitigations
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@glyphtech.ai>, GlyphTech Ops <ops@glyphtech.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Autoscale policy starvation — impact summary and scheduled mitigations

Jordan / GlyphTech ops team —

Apologies for the disruption this morning. Between 08:50–09:05 PDT your dedicated pool for prod-us-west experienced significant queueing and a subset of request streams were paused with server errors (5xx timeouts) while the autoscaler failed to provision additional nodes quickly enough. Root-cause (initial): a recent autoscale policy tweak introduced a secondary "weighting" evaluation which, under a short spike pattern, incorrectly suppressed new node leases when pooled KV cache utilization crossed the 82% threshold. In short: the policy treated steady memory pressure as a signal to delay new allocations rather than trigger scale-out.

What we did immediately:
- Performed manual scale-up to restore capacity (09:01 PDT).
- Applied a temporary policy override to force aggressive provisioning for pools reporting queue depth > 20 and latency > 250ms.
- Captured diagnostic snapshots and the autoscaler metrics window (attached: autoscaler-metrics-20280718.png).

Customer impact:
- Estimated window of degraded throughput: ~15 minutes.
- Number of affected requests: sample indicates ~6k calls experienced elevated latency; a small percentage returned 5xx.
- A small set of long-running batched jobs were paused and retried by your client logic; we preserved logs for those.

Planned remediation and timeline:
1) Hotfix to policy evaluation to remove the secondary suppression rule and add hysteresis (tests complete) — target deploy: 2028-07-19 02:00 UTC (canary first).
2) Add a short-circuit path in the autoscaler to ignore transient spikes in KV cache when queue depth is high — target deploy: 2028-07-21.
3) Update our runbook and add explicit guidance for manual override; automated alerting rule to be tightened immediately.

We will provide a longer post-incident report with exact traces and a proposed SLA credit. In the meantime, attached the key metric snapshot and a draft patch for the policy: autoscale-policy-v2.patch.diff.

If you want a quick call to walk through what happened, I'm available between 11:00–13:00 PDT today. Again — sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as a Sev-2 and will follow up with a full timeline.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0138

Attachments: autoscaler-metrics-20280718.png

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@glyphtech.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale policy starvation — impact summary and scheduled mitigations

Thanks Mina — appreciate the quick mitigation. A few quick questions from our side:

1) Can you confirm whether any inference payloads were dropped vs retried? We had a small number of queued batch jobs that reported retries and I want to reconcile with our logs.
2) Will the hotfix require a maintenance window or restart of our reserved nodes? We prefer minimal disruption; if there is a planned canary please share the cadence.
3) We will expect an SLO credit for the time our production traffic was degraded. What's Redwood's standard for these cases?

If helpful, we can join the 11–13 PDT window — I can be on a short sync at 11:30.

— Jordan
Jordan Lee
Platform Lead, GlyphTech
jordan.lee@glyphtech.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@glyphtech.ai>
Date: 2028-07-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Autoscale policy starvation — ops actions and next steps

Mina / Stephanie — notes and proposed action items after the call: 

- Confirmation: the policy change on 2028-07-17T23:42 UTC added a weighting factor that multiplies cache_utilization by 0.6 when consecutive sampling windows show low eviction rate. That interacted poorly with batched-inference workloads which hold KV for longer.
- Immediate fixes (triage):
  * Push hotfix branch (autoscale-policy-v2.patch.diff) to staging and run the synthetic spike suite (target: within 4 hours).
  * Canary deploy to 10% of pools (start: 2028-07-19T02:00 UTC). Monitor queue depth, scale latency, and 5xx rates.
  * If canary is green for 30m, roll to region. Automatic rollback if 5xx > baseline + 0.5%.
- Communication items:
  * Prepare a customer-facing postmortem with timeline and trace IDs (who owns?): Mina to lead.
  * Draft SLA credit offer template: Stephanie to propose language; suggest pro-rated credit for impacted window plus goodwill credit.
  * Ops runbook change: add a fast-path override when queue_depth > 20 for dedicated pools (I'll PR).

I'll start the staging runs now and report back with results.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Production Services, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@glyphtech.ai>, GlyphTech Ops <ops@glyphtech.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: remediation schedule, runbook changes, and credit offer

Jordan — thanks again for the quick sync this morning. Following our internal validation and the successful canary (10% pools) overnight, here is the consolidated set of deliverables and dates: 

1) Hotfix deployed to canary: 2028-07-19 02:00 UTC — status: PASSED (metrics show scale latency down 65% vs incident window).
2) Full region rollout: scheduled 2028-07-20 03:00 UTC (no restart required; rolling change to autoscaler config only).
3) Runbook updates: PR merged 2028-07-19 15:10 UTC — includes explicit override rules and clearer alert thresholds.
4) Post-incident report: drafting complete; full PDF with trace IDs, metric windows, and timeline available by 2028-07-21 18:00 UTC.
5) SLA credit: attached a proposed credit offer (credit-offer-glyphtech-20280719.pdf). This proposes a pro-rated credit for the impacted 15-minute window plus a one-time goodwill credit for operational disruption. Let us know if that meets your procurement team needs; we can route a formal invoice credit if required.

What we're doing to prevent recurrence:
- Remove suppressive weighting evaluation from policy; replace with conservative hysteresis and short-circuit on sustained queue signals.
- Add a synthetic spike regression in our CI that emulates long-lived KV caches so the policy change is exercised automatically.
- Improve alerting to distinguish memory-pressure-only signals from queue-driven scale needs.

If you'd like a dedicated postmortem call, propose times and we'll schedule. We also preserved full logs and traces for the exact job IDs you mentioned during the incident; if you share those job IDs we can attach the traces to the postmortem.

Apologies again for the disruption. We take this seriously and will follow up with the full report and any additional remediation artifacts.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: autoscale-policy-v2.patch.diff, credit-offer-glyphtech-20280719.pdf
